## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** On the happy path the change does what the description says. Selecting Claude as the default agent, and the new migration for existing Claude-agent installs, both run `omarchy-theme-set-claude --activate`. That writes `"theme": "custom:omarchy"` into `settings.json` under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (default `~/.claude`), keeps the other keys, and publishes `themes/omarchy.json`. The activation happens before Claude Code first launches. The migration does nothing for other agents or when no agent is set. `test/shell.d/default-agent-test.sh` still passes at the head. A trial merge against current `quattro` produced no textual conflict.

Three behaviours are worth a look. They concern existing user choices and failure handling.

### Migration and agent selection replace a theme chosen in Claude Code

`--activate` sets `.theme` unconditionally. The PR now calls it automatically from the migration and on every selection of Claude as the default agent. In sandboxed runs, an existing `light-daltonized` theme (migration) and `light` theme (agent selection) were both replaced with `custom:omarchy`.

The Hermes precedent cited in the description protects an existing choice. `bin/omarchy-theme-set-hermes` changes the skin only when it is unset, `default` or already `omarchy`.

| Existing Claude Code theme | This PR |
|---|---|
| none | set to `custom:omarchy` |
| `dark` (documented default) | replaced |
| `light`, `*-daltonized`, `auto`, another `custom:<slug>` | replaced |

**Impact:** An `omarchy update` silently changes a deliberate Claude Code theme. The echo line is the only notice. Users on a daltonized theme lose that palette, because the generated theme uses a plain dark or light base with red and green status and diff colours.

**Suggested change:** Follow the Hermes rule. Activate only when no theme is set, or when it is the default `dark` or already `custom:omarchy`. Otherwise leave it alone and print how to opt in (`omarchy theme set claude --activate`). The Claude Code settings reference says a legacy `theme` in `~/.claude.json` still applies when no settings file sets one, so a check limited to `settings.json` would still override that value.

### A failed activation stops all later migrations

`omarchy-migrate` runs each migration with `bash -euo pipefail`, stops at the first failure and writes no marker. The new migration exits non-zero in these cases, reproduced in a sandbox:

```text
agent file "claude" with no trailing newline, or empty  -> `read` fails, exit 1
settings.json is not valid JSON                          -> jq parse error, exit 5
generated current/theme/claude.json missing              -> setter exits 1
        |
        v
migration stays pending, later migrations do not run, `omarchy update` stops
(repeats on every retry; each invalid-JSON retry leaves another empty settings.json.XXXXXX)
```

**Impact:** A cosmetic, user-side condition holds back every later migration, including unrelated repairs. Claude Code lets a user continue past a broken `settings.json`, so that condition can persist indefinitely. The missing-source case is narrower on current installs, because an earlier migration (`1787481315.sh`) re-stages themes.

**Suggested change:** Guard the read as `migrations/1786719479.sh` does (`read -r current_agent <"$agent_file" || true`). For user-side problems, report and continue instead of failing. For example, check `jq -e . "$settings"` first, or use `omarchy-theme-set-claude --activate || echo "<hint>"`. Consider a cleanup trap for the setter's temporary file.

### Activation at agent selection fails silently and is never retried

`omarchy-default-agent` runs the setter with `2>/dev/null || true`. When activation fails (for example a missing generated theme or invalid `settings.json`), Claude is still selected and launched with no message. No later automatic path retries it:

```text
migration runs while no agent is set      -> exit 0, marked done
select Claude, activation fails           -> silent, theme not set
next Omarchy theme switch                 -> setter runs without --activate: file copied, settings untouched
omarchy-migrate                           -> nothing pending
```

The same sequence was run in a sandbox. `settings.json` stayed unset until Claude was selected again from the menu.

**Impact:** The theme file keeps syncing, so it looks as if the integration is working, but Claude Code never switches to it. This is the problem the PR sets out to fix.

**Suggested change:** Keep the setter's error output visible in `omarchy-default-agent`. Also consider a Hermes-style step on theme switch: activate when Claude is the Omarchy agent and Claude Code has no theme or the default one. That same rule also covers the first finding.

**Note:** The new comment in `bin/omarchy-default-agent` gives Claude Code's default theme as `"auto"`. The current settings reference lists `"dark"` as the default.
